title: Ukraine defends strikes on Russian ships off Libya as Moscow warns Estonia of 'open war'
dek: Kyiv says its right to self-defence has no geographical limit; Russia accuses Tallinn of letting drones through and the EU proposes cutting 60 more Russian banks from SWIFT.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Ukraine's foreign ministry said on Tuesday that its right to self-defence "is not geographically restricted", a day after President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukrainian naval drones had sunk a Russian corvette in the Libyan port of Benghazi. Russia, meanwhile, accused Estonia of being "on the verge of triggering open war", and the European Commission proposed a 22nd package of sanctions that would cut some 60 more Russian banks off from the SWIFT payments network.

The war on the ground went on. A Russian air raid on Zaporizhzhia at dawn on Tuesday killed two people and injured about 40, including an infant, regional officials said, and a drone strike on the railway station in Korosten in the Zhytomyr region killed one person. Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 96 drones overnight, of which 73 were shot down or jammed. Russia's defence ministry said it had destroyed 699 Ukrainian drones over seven regions, Crimea and the Black Sea; the two sides' figures cover different attacks and cannot be independently verified.

## The Libya strikes

Mr Zelensky said on Monday that seven Ukrainian-built naval drones attacked Russian vessels on Sunday, sinking the corvette Merkury while it was docked in Benghazi, destroying a Ka-27 helicopter and hitting the cargo ship Angara, which he said was carrying weapons. He called it an "exemplary Ukrainian operation". Russian officials had not commented on the loss of the warship by Tuesday evening, though Moscow has warned Kyiv of a "dangerous trend" after attacks on its ships off Libya and in the Baltic.

Eastern Libyan authorities, who control Benghazi, said Libya "is not a party to the Russian-Ukrainian war". Saddam Haftar, deputy commander of the eastern forces, said they "firmly reject the use of our territory or territorial waters as an arena for settling scores". The UN mission in Libya called for "an immediate, independent and transparent investigation".

Ukraine's foreign ministry spokesman, Heorhii Tykhyi, cited Article 51 of the UN Charter and said Russian warships, cargo ships carrying military equipment and "shadow fleet" tankers were legitimate targets wherever they are. "Ukraine's actions are directed solely against the aggressor and are not aimed at any third party," he said. Germany's defence minister, Boris Pistorius, said Ukraine has the right to strike military targets in Russia but that the war must not spread to the Baltic Sea.

## Estonia and the EU

Russia's foreign ministry summoned Estonia's charge d'affaires in Moscow on Monday to protest Estonia's decision to close its border crossings with Russia from 1 December for at least six months. It accused Tallinn of "tacitly" letting Ukrainian drones use its airspace and of obstructing Russian shipping, and said the closure "will inevitably backfire" on Estonia and its EU and NATO allies. Estonia's foreign ministry replied that it "has never allowed, and will never allow, its territory to be used for military operations by another country". Estonia announced the closure after accusing Russian security services of an attempted arson attack on an Estonian defence company, which Moscow denies.

The Commission's proposal, presented by President Ursula von der Leyen on Monday, would extend a full transaction ban to about 60 Russian banks, bar oil tankers insured in Russia from EU ports, extend the ban on energy services to cover refineries and electricity, ban Russian teams and athletes from competing under the Russian flag at events in the EU, and deny visas to people who have served in Russia's armed forces since the invasion. It also targets third countries that help Russia evade sanctions, without naming them. "Sporting events must not be allowed to become a platform for propaganda," Ms von der Leyen said. The package needs the approval of all 27 member states.

## Why it matters for India

Earlier EU packages have listed entities in India and other third countries accused of supplying Russia's military, and have restricted imports of fuels refined from Russian crude. Indian refiners and exporters will be watching the final text for any new third-country listings. EU leaders meet on 26-27 November, when Ukraine's funding needs for 2027 are also on the agenda. Hungary's new prime minister, Peter Magyar, travelled to western Ukraine on Tuesday for his first visit as head of government.
